abstract: Summary form only given. Investigations of a two photon polymerization technique and its potential for the fabrication of low-loss, high-performance microoptical devices will be discussed. The resins we use are designed for ultraviolet photolithography and contain photo-initiators sensitive to 390 nm radiation. These resins are exposed to tightly focused 80-fs Ti:sapphire laser pulses initiating two-photon polymerization in small focal volume.

articleTitle: Optical characteristics of 2D air-glass and metal-glass photonic superlattice crystals
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. The superlattice 2D structures investigated were produced using multiple drawing technique from the tubes prepared from optical glass. For air-glass structures the stacks containing some dozens of cylindrical hollow tubes forming hexagonal structure placed in the glass envelope was used. For metal glass structure we use stacks made from 10 X 10 glass tubes filled with low-temperature melted metal (Pb-Sn mixture). The microphotograph of this structure is shown.

articleTitle: Ultra-sensitive milliwatt peak power pulse characterization via wavelength conversion frequency resolved optical gating in optical fiber
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. We report a new FROG geometry using wavelength conversion in optical fiber which has been used to characterize 1 mW peak power, 20 ps pulses from an unamplified semiconductor laser. We use a novel configuration whereby a pulsed pump is mixed with a CW signal to generate an idler We thus obtain an effective second-order nonlinear response that can be used to generate a FROG trace.

articleTitle: Excess noise in optical pulses in non-Hermitian mode-locked laser systems
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. We present a comprehensive fully quantum mechanical model, with self-consistent numerical simulations, for the noise in optical pulses in both linear and non-linear (including dynamic gain/loss saturation) mode-locked laser systems in which the time evolution operator for the pulse fluctuations is not Hermitian. Our results show that the excess noise factor can be quite large. In semiconductor mode-locked lasers this factor can exceed 10 for the mean square timing and frequency noise. We construct quantum mechanical operators for the pulse photon number, phase, frequency and timing fluctuations, and show that in non-Hermitian systems these fluctuation operators have first order contributions from eigen-modes of all order. This is a novel result since in Hermitian mode-locked systems to first order only the first two eigen-modes contribute to these fluctuation operators. We also show that the spectra of the pulse energy and timing fluctuations obtained by measuring the spectrum of the photo-detector current noise are exactly the spectra of the energy and timing fluctuation operators that we construct, and contain significant contributions from higher order eigen-modes.

articleTitle: Suppression of pattern distortion in semiconductor optical amplifier by using fiber loop mirror
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. An interferometric approach for pulse pattern effect reduction in SOAs is proposed and demonstrated. Suppression of waveform distortion is achieved by using a fiber loop mirror. Over 5-dB input power dynamic range enhancement is obtained.

articleTitle: Vertically stacking 10 periods of self-assembled InAs/InP quantum wires
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. Additional confinement in semiconductor quantum wires is expected to significantly improve the performances of semiconductor devices due to the increased density of states at the band edge. We report our result on the fabrication of self-assembled InAs/InP quantum wires (QWRs) with single and 10 vertical-periods. Our InAs QWRs were grown on InP [001] substrates in a Riber 32 MBE system at the temperature of 430/spl deg/C and a growth rate of 0.3 ML/s. The photoluminescence (PL) spectra and PL polarizations of the two samples were investigated at different pump wavelengths, different pump intensities and sample temperatures. Our results exhibited unique behaviors, especially on the stacked quantum wires. Following our detailed analyses, we determined the structure of the stacked quantum wires from the bottom to the top, which is different from the designed one. Furthermore, we have provided a new design that will result in the narrowing of the PL linewidth for the stacked self-assembled quantum wires.

articleTitle: LP/sub 02/-mode dispersion compensation using a noble hollow core fiber mode converter
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. In this paper, we report the LP/sub 02/ mode dispersion-compensating scheme based on a hollow optical fiber mode converter (HOF-MC) in a ring-core index dispersion compensating fiber (DCF) in order to couple to the LP/sub 02/ mode more efficiently. Since the MC is based on an adiabatic transformation of the guided mode without a periodic structure, it is inherently robust against environmental influences and could be spliced to conventional single-mode fibers (SMFs) with low loss. Design parameters of both the ring core DCF and the mating MC are discussed to optimize average compensated dispersion and dispersion slope in the conventional band (C-band, 1.53-1.57 /spl mu/m) of erbium-doped-fiber amplifiers (EDFAs), and the differential modal delay between LP/sub 01/ and LP/sub 02/ modes is also analyzed.

articleTitle: Tm/sup 3+/ spectroscopy and amplifier performance of antimony silicate glasses
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. Antimony silicates are surprisingly good hosts for Tm/sup 3+/ for 14 xx applications. Compositional dependencies of thulium spectroscopy and 14 xx emission lifetimes will be reviewed, and the performance of Tm-doped antimony silicate gain media will be discussed.

articleTitle: Photonic band gap materials: a semiconductor for light
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. I review and discuss the role of three-dimensional light localization in the development of integrated optics on a photonic crystal micro-chip. The control and selective inhibition of spontaneous emission in a three dimensional photonic band gap material offers the possibility of developing novel active devices on such a chip.

articleTitle: Terahertz semiconductor-heterostructure lasers
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Injection lasers based on interminiband transitions in GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructures are operated in the THz range. Single-mode emission is achieved at 4.4THz, with output powers of 2.5mW and thresholds of few hundred A/cm/sup 2/ up to 50K.

articleTitle: Time-lens timing-jitter compensator in ultra-long haul DWDM dispersion managed soliton transmissions
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: A time lens based on clock-driven phase modulators followed by linear dispersion accurately removes timing-jitter. When used prior to the receiver, the time lens greatly improves bit-error-rate performance in DWDM dispersion managed soliton transmissions.

articleTitle: 135W CW fiber laser with perfect single mode output
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Reliable 135 W CW ytterbium doped fiber laser has been demonstrated with measured M/sup 2/ < 1.05. The stimulated Raman scattering imposed the major limit on the output power. No thermal distortions or damage of the fiber core was observed.

articleTitle: Enhanced 40-Gbit/s receiver sensitivity with all-fiber optical 2R regenerator
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. We demonstrate an all-fiber optical 2R regenerator (02R) integrated with a tunable, low-dispersion fiber Bragg grating (FBG) filter. We show that such device can significantly improve the sensitivity and optical signal to noise ratio (OSNR) degradation tolerance of a 40 Gbit/s receiver.

articleTitle: Novel guided-wave single-sideband electrooptic modulators by using periodically domain-inverted structure
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. We propose novel guided-wave electrooptic single sideband (SSB) modulators consisting of a pair of traveling-wave electrodes and a Mach-Zehnder waveguide. Adopting the periodically domain-inverted structure with a spatial shift to LiNbO/sub 3/ or LiTaO/sub 3/ traveling-wave modulators, the modulation phase and the modulation index can be controlled arbitrary so that the SSB modulation characteristics are obtained with one microwave modulation signal and a DC bias signal.

articleTitle: Demonstration of a radiatively cooled laser
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. We have developed a new optical pumping technique that minimizes the thermal loading in a solid-state laser system. This technique incorporates optical cooling directly into a laser medium. Lasing conditions were studied in which the waste heat required by stimulated emission is offset by cooling from anti-Stokes spontaneous emission. We call this condition a radiation balanced laser. Under ideal conditions, the heat load within the lasing medium can be completely eliminated. Perturbation analysis of the RBL condition reveals that thermal loads in the range of 5 W/cm/sup 3/ should be obtainable in scalable solid-state laser designs such as for Yb:KGd(WO/sub 4/)/sub 2/ lasers.

articleTitle: Radiation effects on a two-stage double-pass single-polarization erbium fiber amplifier
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. In free space communication, it is desirable to have single-polarization EDFAs since polarization diversity can be used to multiplex transmitter and receiver or double transmitter capacity per wavelength via polarization diplexing. In this paper, we use the double-pass Faraday mirror approach to realize a 250 mW single-polarization EDFA, without the need for special polarization controllers or maintaining Er fibers.

articleTitle: Impact of photodetector nonlinearities on photonic analog-to-digital converters
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. Photodetector nonlinearities can limit the performance of high-dynamic-range analog optical systems. For systems that use short optical pulses to process or transmit analog information, this limitation is magnified due to the higher peak intensity at the photodetector input. In this paper, we examine the trade-off between signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and linearity in optically sampled analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) due to saturation of the photodetector responsivity.

articleTitle: 10 W widely tunable narrow linewidth double-clad fiber ring laser
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. We report on a widely tunable narrow linewidth ytterbium-doped fiber ring laser device with a linearly polarized output power of 10 W. The Large Mode Area (LMA) core of the 20 m long fiber had a diameter of 10 /spl mu/m and was doped with 1000 ppm ytterbium. The core was transverse single-mode for wavelengths above 1 /spl mu/m. The pump-cladding was D-shaped in order to improve the pump light absorption. As pump source we used a fiber coupled 980 nm laser diode. The small quantum defect between the pump and the laser wavelength enables a very high efficiency. At maximum pump power of nearly 32 W a linearly polarized output power of 10 W with a slope efficiency of 68% with respect to the absorbed pump power at a wavelength of 1080 nm was achieved.

articleTitle: Tunable THz-wave generation in DAST crystal by nonlinear difference frequency mixing
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. We successfully demonstrate widely tunable and high frequency THz-wave generation in the range of 1.5 to 6.5 THz with thin DAST crystals for the first time. We show an arrangement for THz-wave generation in DAST by mixing dual wavelengths of KTiOPO/sub 4/ optical parametric oscillator which has two KTP crystals in the same cavity.

articleTitle: 150 W Nd/Yb codoped fiber laser at 1.1 /spl mu/m
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. We report on a neodymium-ytterbium-codoped fiber which can be pumped at two separated diode laser wavelengths (808 nm and 940 nm). The combined output at 1.1 /spl mu/m represents a scalability of double-clad fiber lasers by a factor of 2.

articleTitle: High-speed wavelength switching by using an optical single-sideband modulator
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. Wavelength conversion by using an optical single sideband (SSB) electro optical modulator has very high-speed switching time and can be applied for high-speed WDM switching such as packet-switching.

articleTitle: Electrostatic and piezoelectric analog tunable diffractive gratings
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. We show a tunable MEMS grating design which permits analog control over the diffraction angle. This is accomplished by analog actuation of the grating beams in the lateral direction. Compared to other tunable grating implementations (e.g. the grating light valve and the polychromator), our device trades deflection range for angular resolution. Applications for high resolution analog tunable gratings include microspectrometers, external cavity tunable lasers, and thermal compensators for wavelength multiplexer-demultiplexers. in this paper, we describe two implementations: electrostatic and piezoelectric.

articleTitle: Q-switched 980 nm Yb-doped fiber laser
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. Here, we present a Q-switched 980 nm cladding-pumped YDFL with 1.2 /spl mu/J of energy and 60 W of peak power in pulses shorter than 20 ns at repetition rates of up to /spl sim/0.2 MHz and 250 mW of average output power for repetition rates between 0.2 and 0.65 MHz. A pulsed 980 nm source with high peak power and good beam quality is attractive for frequency conversion, e.g. frequency quadrupling to 245 nm.

articleTitle: Performance enhancement of an optical interconnect using short pulses from a modelocked diode laser
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. We have demonstrated a short-pulse optical interconnect that uses a practical, high-repetition-rate modelocked source. BER measurements show that operation with short pulses improves system performance by providing a receiver sensitivity enhancement of 3.3 dB. The link has additional benefits related to timing issues and latency reduction.

articleTitle: Single-channel 800 Gbit/s asynchronous all-optical amplitude-division demultiplexing based on polarization-independent GHz Raman soliton in fiber
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: We demonstrate error-free asynchronous all-optical time-division and amplitude-division demultiplexing based on polarization-independent TDM-WDM conversion, which realizes an intensity-dependent self-frequency shift in GHz Raman soliton. An 800 Gbit/s (128 /spl times/ 6.3 Gbit/s) optical TDM signal is simultaneously demultiplexed to 6.3 Gbit/s multiple-channel signals. We demultiplex a random data signal with a time slot of narrower than 800 fs corresponding to a 1.28 Tbit/s OTDM signal. Furthermore, our demultiplexer is capable of demultiplexing from overlapping OTDM signals with 2.0 ps pulse width and 780 fs time delay.

articleTitle: Frequency-domain phase-conjugate femtosecond pulse generation using frequency resolved cross-phase modulation
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. We have demonstrated generation of a temporally reversed femtosecond pulse inside chirped pulse system. Frequency chirping in an input pulse due to unknown group velocity dispersion is converted to opposite frequency chirping by this scheme. This opposite chirped pulse, a frequency domain phase conjugation pulse, reconstructs the initial phase structure after propagating through the same dispersion medium. We can automatically compensate phase distortion of an ultrashort and/or ultrabroadband light pulse.

articleTitle: A cw kW- class diode end pumped Nd:YAG slab laser
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: This report deals with a diode end pumped slablaser with an average cw output power of 982W and 39% efficiency. The beam quality of the hybrid resonator is superior to Mk7.

articleTitle: Characteristics of all-optical 2R regenerators based on self-phase modulation in high-nonlinear fibers
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. All-optical re-amplification and re-shaping (2R) is a key technology that enables long distance transmission of high-bit-rate data. A simple all-optical 2R scheme was proposed by Mamyshev (1998) This 2R scheme is based on self-phase-modulation (SPM) in a fiber and a subsequent optical filtering at a shifted frequency. The amplitude fluctuations in "0s" and "1s" can be effectively suppressed. Although simple in concept, several important questions need to be answered: (i) what is the optimum fiber length and dispersion; (ii) how to minimize power budget; and (iii) what is the limitation due to stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS). The SBS effect should be considered in the SPM based spectral broadening process. We propose two 2R regeneration designs. Dithering the transmitter laser frequency effectively broadens the pulse spectral bandwidth and increases SBS threshold in the first design. The second design uses an isolator to connect two high-nonlinear fibers, HNLF-1 and HNLF-2. The dispersion of HNLF-2 can be smaller so the extra loss introduced by the isolator can be tolerated.

articleTitle: Tunable dual-/spl lambda/ fiber ring laser based on 2/sup nd/ order Sagnac-Lyot fiber filter
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. We have successfully demonstrated a tunable dual-wavelength fiber laser based on unique 2/sup nd/ order Sagnac-Lyot filters. These filters provide absolute wavelength tuning, channel spacing tuning and stable dual-wavelength lasing.

articleTitle: Space qualification of the Geoscience Laser Altimeter System (GLAS) laser transmitters
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. We have completed the manufacture, space-qualification and delivery of three flight, diode pumped solid-state lasers for the Geoscience Laser Altimeter System (GLAS), the sole instrument for the ICESat (ice, cloud and land elevation satellite) mission scheduled to launch in early 2002.

articleTitle: Parametric interactions between pumps and signals in a co-pumped Raman amplifier
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. Distributed Raman amplification can increase transmission distance and is essential for high bit-rate (10 Gb/s and higher) systems. Counter-pumped Raman amplification is preferable because the relative intensity noise (RIN) transferred from pump to signal is less than that of co-pumped Raman amplification. However, recent studies show that combining co-pumped Raman amplification with counter-pumped Raman amplification helps to increase optical signal-to-noise ratio (OSNR). In this paper, we report the parametric interactions between pumps and signals that could be harmful in co-pumped Raman amplification and should be taken into account during the design of Raman amplifiers.

articleTitle: Temporal gain variations in time-division multiplexed Raman pumping schemes
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: We implemented a single-wavelength, pulsed Raman pump with several Watts of output power, widely variable duty cycle and repetition rate, and 12 dB extinction ratio (maximum power/minimum power) using a cascaded Raman fiber lasers at 1465 nm that was modulated by a LiNbO/sub 3/ Mach-Zehnder modulator and passed through a dual stage, high-power cascaded Raman fiber amplifier (CRA).

articleTitle: Residual phase noise and longitudinal mode linewidth measurements of hybridly modelocked external cavity semiconductor diode laser
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. We report measurements of residual phase noise knee position and average linewidth of a hybrid modelocked external cavity semiconductor laser. We show that the knee position in our laser linearly increases with cavity frequency and is determined by the average longitudinal mode linewidth. This suggests that, to attain ultra-low jitter modelocked lasers, methods for reducing the longitudinal mode linewidth are needed.

articleTitle: Optical Q-factor monitoring at 160 Gb/s using an optical sampling system in an 80 km transmission experiment
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. In-service quality monitoring of high bit-rate optical transmission systems can be achieved at the full line rate by using optical sampling systems. Here, we report on the quantitative evaluation of 160 Gb/s eye diagrams measured after 80 km of fiber transmission.

articleTitle: High-power diode-pumped Yb:KGW ultrafast laser
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. We present a simple passively modelocked diode-pumped Yb:KGd(WO/sub 4/)/sub 2/ (Yb:KGW) laser. We achieved pulses as short as 150 fs and an average output power of 1.5 W by using a 15 W fiber-coupled laser diode to pump the laser crystal, and a semiconductor saturable absorber mirror (SESAM) to initiate passive mode locking.

articleTitle: All-optical 3R regeneration using an ultrafast polarization bistable VCSEL
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. A VCSEL with In/sub 0.2/Ga/sub 0.8/As active layers and AlAs/GaAs DBR mirrors was used in the experiment. A novel all-optical 3R regeneration using an ultrafast polarization bistable VCSEL has been proposed. We are now conducting the experiments on such 3R regeneration at 10 Gbit/s.

articleTitle: Diffraction-limited, 300-kW-peak-power pulses from a Yb-doped fiber amplifier
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. We demonstrate that bend loss-induced mode filtering is effective in scaling large-core-area fiber amplifiers to significantly higher pulse energies and peak powers while maintaining diffraction-limited beam quality, high repetition rates, and transform-limited temporal and spectral profiles. This system provides the highest single-transverse-mode pulse energy, peak power, and average power simultaneously extracted from a fiber amplifier to date.

articleTitle: Polymer waveguide optical interconnections for electrical interconnection substrates
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. An integration process and measured result of a fully embedded thin film MSM photodetector (PD) fabricated from InGaAs which is embedded in a polymer optical waveguide which is deposited on a Si substrate is presented, thus realizing the goal of three separate, independently optimized materials for the waveguide, substrate, and PD. The dark current and photocurrent produced by the evanescent field coupling from the optical waveguide into the embedded MSM PD are shown Measured dark and photocurrent were 60.6 nA and 1.2 /spl mu/A at 5 V, respectively. The coupling efficiency was estimated based on the measured responsivity and photocurrent of the thin film MSM PD and the launched optical power was calculated using a mode matching approach through FIMMWAVE software from Photon Design. The estimated coupling efficacy from the input optical waveguide to the embedded MSM PD was 71.74%.

articleTitle: 1480 nm two-cascaded highly efficient Raman fiber laser
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. Lasers based on high P/sub 2/O/sub 5/-doped fibers can potentially have a higher efficiency than Raman fiber lasers (RFL) based on standard Ge-doped fibers. An increase of phosphorus content in the fiber core gives rise to an increase of the Raman gain coefficient. Despite a rise of optical losses, heavily P/sub 2/O/sub 5/-doped fibers enable one to develop extremely efficient Raman lasers. A two-cascaded Raman laser based on a P/sub 2/O/sub 5/-doped fiber with the frequency shift of 1330 cm/sup -1/ per cascade and with Bragg gratings written directly in the P/sub 2/O/sub 5/-doped fiber demonstrated the highest ever achieved efficiency in RFL.

articleTitle: Measurements of beat length in short low-birefringence fibers
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. We show a simple technique for birefringence measurements based on a fiber optic loop mirror (FOLM). We demonstrate birefringence measurements in fiber spans as short as 0.07 of a beat length. To measure fiber birefringence, we twisted the fiber and observed the dependence of the FOLM transmission on the fiber twist. The fine-adjustment of birefringence of one of the ports was needed in measurements. The adjustment mechanism produces low-birefringence by applying pressure over a fiber section of several millimeters and rotates the principal axes of this section.

articleTitle: Polymer micro-ring modulator with 1 THz FSR
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Polymer microring modulators with FSR larger than 1 THz, modulation bandwidth of 15 GHz and the fall with half maximum voltage of 20 V are demonstrated at 1300 nm. Multi-wavelength modulation with a total bandwidth of 400 Gb/s is practical.

articleTitle: High power external cavity semiconductor laser with wavelength tuning over C, L, and S-bands using single-angled-facet gain chip
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: An InP-based single-angled-facet (SAF) gain chip comprised of a curved ridge waveguide is used to make an external cavity semiconductor laser. Wide wavelength tuning over C, L, and S-bands (155 nm) is demonstrated with an output power of more than 80 mW over the entire tuning range and a peak output power of 130 mW.

articleTitle: 1kW CW output from fiber-embedded disk lasers
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. The fiber-embedded disk was made in a spiral mode fabrication by a square fiber laser with Nd-doped fiber core. The disk is available for the planer waveguide which can propagate the pumping power. The fiber disk laser keeps the same principle as the double clad fiber lasers as follows. 1) The lasing beam is confined in the fiber core. 2) The pumping power is also confined inside the planer waveguide. 3) The cooling efficiency is very good and it is a half of the typical fiber lasers.

articleTitle: Direct 880 nm diode-pumping of vanadate lasers
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. We have demonstrated, what we believe is for the first time, direct diode-pumping of end-pumped vanadate lasers such as Nd:YVO/sub 4/ lasers. Scaling to TEM/sub 00/ mode powers in excess of 20 W is currently being investigated. Results for higher pump powers and for dual end-pumping will be presented.

articleTitle: High-average-power millijoule fiber amplifier system
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. We report for the first time to our knowledge on a multi millijoule system with repetition rates in the 10 kHz range. The setup of the high power and high energy Yb-doped fiber amplifier is shown. As a nanosecond seed source a Q-switched Nd:YAG disk laser is applied the laser delivers average powers up to 2.5 W.

articleTitle: Passively mode-locked surface-emitting semiconductor laser with nearly 1 W average power
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. We recently demonstrated the first continuously pumped and passively mode-locked vertical-external-cavity surface-emitting laser (VECSEL). This laser was mode-locked with a semiconductor saturable absorber mirror (SESAM). Now we present as much as 950 mW in 15-ps pulses. The repetition rate was also increased to 6 GHz.

articleTitle: Novel design of polarization splitter based on a quasi-state multimode interference coupler
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. We introduced the quasi-state using four-mode interference in the multimode interference (MMI) coupler. For TE polarization, output powers at the bar and cross waveguides are shown as a function of the propagation length, and quasistates are depicted.

articleTitle: All-optical timing extraction with simultaneous optical demultiplexing using time-dependent loss saturation in electro-absorption modulator
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Counter propagation between data and clock pulses inside the optically controlled EAM is used for all-optical timing extraction and demultiplexing. Demultiplexing from 4OGbit/s showed error free operation with I 200 fs jitter for the recovered clock.

articleTitle: A novel wavelength dividing and switching device using arrayed waveguides
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. Optical space switching - the rearrangement of the optical paths in a network - can provide the greater flexibility and reliability required for managing high-bandwidth networks. As a new optical space switching device, we have proposed an optical wavelength switching device using arrayed waveguides that have different refractive index by MOVPE selective area growth based on InGaAs/InP MQW structures.

articleTitle: 4.2 W Cr/sup 2+/:ZnSe face cooled disk laser
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. We have shown that the face-cooled disk laser can effectively reduce thermal effects in Cr/sup 2+/ lasers by demonstrating a 4.2-W, Cr/sup 2+/:ZnSe, face-cooled disk laser with output power limited only by the available pump power. The difficulty of compensating for thermal lensing inside a resonator is traded for the less difficult task of efficiently absorbing the pump laser in a thin laser crystal.

articleTitle: Experimental determination of heat flow in semiconductor lasers
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. The investigation of heat flow in a semiconductor laser diode performed here leads to the conclusion that a thermal probe is useful for parameter extraction; the model used, however, must be quite detailed in devices with low wallplug efficiency.

articleTitle: Blue light and infrared continuum generation in a highly nonlinear holey fiber
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. Holey fibers (HF) are very attractive for the realization of all-optical fiber devices based on nonlinear phenomena. We have investigated the nonlinear behaviour of a HF characterized by a very small effective area that enhances its nonlinear properties and by a strong asymmetry in the core region that induces a high birefringence, leading to a polarization maintaining behaviour. Our experimental results are obtained by coupling a 110 fs pulse train at 1.55 /spl mu/m (80 MHz repetition rate) generated by an optical parametric oscillator (OPO) in a 55 cm long HF span.

articleTitle: Reduction of mode partition noise in a multiwavelength semiconductor laser through hybrid modelocking
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. The longitudinal modes of a multimode laser diode suffer from intensity fluctuations that, when coupled with spectral filtering, result in mode partition noise (MPN). We have significantly decreased the MPN in a modelocked, multiwavelength semiconductor laser. A gain-guided GaAs-AlGaAs semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA) is inserted in an external cavity which incorporates a spectrometer and binary amplitude spatial filter to define individual wavelength channels. Our method exploits the saturable nonlinearity in a multiple-quantum-well (MQW) saturable absorber, along with high speed gain modulation, to establish hybrid modelocking in the external cavity semiconductor diode laser. The result is an error-free optical pulse train in each of the wavelength channels generated by the multiwavelength laser.

articleTitle: High data rate (10 Gbit/sec) demonstration in holographic disk digital data storage system
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. In digital holographic data storage data modulation coding, data interleaving, and error correction are usually implemented in addition to conventional holography and multiplexing. The performance of the holographic disk digital data storage system is determined by several major factors, most notably, by the optical parameters (such as the imaging NA), material performance (dynamic range or M/#, scattering, and thickness), as well as available laser power.

articleTitle: ASE and laser emission in double-clad EDTF
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. We present a detailed study of emission properties of newly fabricated double-clad Er/sup 3+/-doped tellurite single mode fibers. Using a 980 nm pump, a spectrally very broad erbium amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) is observed around 1.5 micron and, at sufficiently high powers, resonance lines are seen at the peak of the ASE curve. Fibers of different lengths have been measured and all found to laze efficiently in the 1530-1600 nm range. Both ASE and the laser lines shift to longer wavelengths with increasing fiber length. Tellurite glass fibers appear to facilitate radiative transitions over a broad spectral range.

articleTitle: Adaptive multiresolution split-step wavelet collocation method for nonlinear optical pulse propagation
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. Pulse propagation in a nonlinear optical medium is described by the nonlinear Schrodinger equation (NLSE). For large wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) systems, the simulation time can run into weeks. We developed a new, flexible, fast and adaptive split-step wavelet collocation method (SSWCM) which provides a substantial speed-up compared to the standard split-step Fourier method (SSFM).

articleTitle: Master-oscillator-power-amplifier laser with adaptive aberration correction
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. The master oscillator is a diode-pumped, almost diffraction limited Nd:YVO/sub 4/ laser. We used a birefringence-compensation scheme consisting of relay-imaging telescope with two lenses and a quartz-rotator to eliminate the stress-induced birefringence of the two Nd:YAG amplifiers. This birefringence and the resulting depolarization is the strongest aberration in Nd:YAG lasers.

articleTitle: Wavelength beam combining of ytterbium fiber lasers in a MOPA configuration
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. There is an increasing interest in combining large numbers of relatively low-power lasers to produce much more powerful, high-brightness laser beams. Coherent combining and wavelength (spectral) combining are the two main approaches being studied. We have been concentrating on wavelength beam combining with fiber lasers and have previously demonstrated this concept at low power. Here we discuss recent work to extend this idea to a master-oscillator power-amplifier (MOPA) configuration by adding a power amplification stage to each oscillator fiber and demonstrating recombination at higher powers.

articleTitle: Near diffraction limited high-contrast 10 terawatt laser
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. We report on further progress in developing a Ti:sapphire high contrast laser, namely reaching a 10 TW milestone. Large output energy of the regenerative amplifier allows us to do this by amplifying the regenerative amplifier output pulse in a single 4-pass amplifier.

articleTitle: Hollow-fiber OP-CPA for energetic ultrafast ultraviolet pulse generation
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. We address the energy scaling through the application of optical parametric chirped pulse amplification (OPCPA) technique to hollow-core fiber frequency conversion. A narrow-band short-wavelength pump pulse is mixed with a longer wavelength wide-band pulse, chirped to match the pulse duration of the pump.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of a timing jitter eater
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. We have demonstrated 4 dB of timing jitter reduction of a semiconductor mode locked laser. Optimal designs for telecommunication applications and optical sampling applications will be discussed as well as performance improvements with solitons.

articleTitle: Self-imaging waveguide Nd:YAG laser with 58% slope efficiency
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. We have demonstrated self-imaging 1D and 2D Nd:YAG lasers and amplifiers based on 100 /spl mu/m/spl times/10 mm rectangular aperture waveguides. A thin layer of 0.8% doped Nd:YAG is diffusion-bonded to sapphire cladding layers to give a 1D waveguide with a numerical aperture of 0.47. 2D confinement is then provided by additional gain-guiding in the horizontal plane.

articleTitle: Nanostructured polymeric optical limiter materials
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. A new type of nonlinear nano-layered polymeric optical limiter material is described. The specific materials described here comprise 4096 alternating polymer layers with an average layer thickness of about 90 nm and another with an average layer thickness near 31 nm. A nonlinear response is introduced by including an appropriate dye in alternate polymer layers. The nonlinear nano-layered materials possess a modulation in the nonlinear refractive index in the direction normal to the surface. When the layer thickness is approximately a quarter wavelength, the new materials correspond to a dielectric stack where the refractive index difference between the layers is intensity dependent. Such materials have several uses including particular optical limiting. Several nano-layered materials using optical limiter dyes in alternate layers were fabricated. The response time for the reflectivity change in a 91 nm nanolayered polymer dyed with PbPc(CP)/sub 4/ was of the order of 1 picosecond.

articleTitle: A new versatile Nd:glass 200 J facility: ALISE; or from monochromatic and smoothed nanosecond pulses towards the ultra-intense femtosecond regime
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. The ALISE facility is a new power chain constructed in the CEA-CESTA. We distinguish three main stages: the frontend, the power chain, and the experimental rooms (target chamber and laser experiments). The femtosecond pulses are Ti:sapphire technology stretched to 2 ns and amplified up to few mJ by a Ti:sapphire regenerative laser amplifier. The preamplifier module is a diode pumped Nd:glass regenerative amplifier.

articleTitle: Novel solution for transient control of WDM amplifiers using the combination of electrical feedforward and feedback
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. We present a practical and low cost EDFA control solution in which both electrical feedforward and feedback are employed. We have demonstrated that with this automatic gain control technology the gain excursion happening in WDM systems can be drastically reduced.

articleTitle: Novel optical fiber dispersion monitor using optical single sideband modulation
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. We propose a novel method of GVD measurement using optical single sideband (SSB) modulation. In the proposed method, we alternate the sideband of the probe light between upper and lower frequency sides, and determine the GVD value from the phase shift induced by the alternation of the sideband. The accuracy and dynamic range of this method is high, and the sign as well as the absolute value of the GVD can be measured only from the output light without any extra procedures.

articleTitle: Efficient, high-repetition rate, blue source using a compact Cr:LiSAF laser
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. We report a compact, directly diode-pumped Cr:LiSAF laser as an alternative pump source. This laser has an electrical-to-optical efficiency in excess of 1% and produces transform-limited pulses of /spl sim/150 fs in duration at /spl sim/865 nm. The average power is 35 mW and the repetition rate is /spl sim/250 MHz, which implies modest peak powers of less than 1 kW. At these low power levels, efficient frequency doubling usually requires complex arrangements, especially if the pulse duration is to be preserved. In this paper we describe the use of a relatively thick doubling crystal in a single-pass, extra-cavity arrangement. Although the second harmonic pulses suffer temporal broadening, this represents an effective way to achieve efficient frequency conversion in a simplified configuration. The nonlinear crystal was potassium niobate (KNbO/sub 3/) cut for non-critical phase matching at 860 nm and 22/spl deg/C.

articleTitle: Generation of UV light from microstructured fibers pumped with femtosecond 800 nm oscillator
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. We report the observation of the upconversion of the femtosecond 800 nm pulses from a commercial Ti:sapphire oscillator to the UV frequency range. It is unambiguously observed that the nonlinear mechanism is distinct from that of the supercontinuum generation and the UV generation occurs starting from the higher-order mode at the fundamental wavelength and yielding a very high-order mode in the UV. The efficiency of the UV generation was found to be strongly dependent on the polarization of the fundamental and varied between experiments. These findings strongly suggest that launching the fundamental light into a higher-order mode was critical for the process. The aforementioned threshold corresponds to the melting of the fiber tip after which the tip is no longer flat but rather works as a phase mask for the coupling of the input light. Such a mask decreases the efficiency of the fundamental mode excitation leading to the disappearance of the supercontinuum and increases the efficiency of higher-mode excitation which results in the UV generation through phase matching to even higher-order modes.

articleTitle: High-speed all-optical signal processing in optical communication systems
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. The transmission capacity of the fiber is expanded by increasing both the number of wavelength channels (wavelength-division multiplexing, WDM) and the bit rate per WDM-channel (time-division multiplexing, TDM). A channel bit rate of 40 Gbit/s will soon be installed and the next generation TDM bit rate of 160 Gbit/s is under active study in several research laboratories. As electrical signal processing is not available at 160 Gbit/s today, the TDM bit rate of 160 Gbit/s requires the optical time division multiplexing (OTDM) technique. In this paper, we report on components and techniques enabling 160 Gbit/s OTDM transmission. We focus on semiconductor based devices.

articleTitle: CW and pulsed Cr/sup 2+/:ZnS and ZnSe microchip lasers
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. There is a growing demand for affordable, compact, room temperature operational and broadly tunable mid-infrared laser sources for use in a variety of remote sensing applications. The most impressive results have been obtained using Cr/sup 2+/:ZnSe crystals. Cr:ZnS and especially Cr:CdS have yet remained barely studied. In this paper we extend our effort to develop novel high optical density and high quality chromium doped ZnS, CdS, and ZnSe microchip laser crystals.

articleTitle: Statistical evaluation of polarization-dependent losses and polarization-mode dispersion in an installed fiber network
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. We compare measured histograms of the installed fibers to simple simulations that indicate that the network under test does not conform with the results of these simple simulations.

articleTitle: 10 Gb/s operation of optical preamplifier using inverted ASE signal of saturated semiconductor optical amplifier
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. Semiconductor optical amplifiers (SOAs) are attractive for use in metro optical networks as well as in access networks. We proposed an optical preamplifier using the optical modulation of ASE in a saturated SOA. The proposed preamplifier only needs a single connection between a fiber and the SOA, which relaxes requirements on AR coating and assembling with a single mode fiber. In addition, this preamplifier can potentially avoid using a narrow-band optical filter. In this paper, we investigate the high-speed response of the preamplifier and demonstrate 10 Gb/s operation. In our proposed preamplifier, an input signal is converted to the modulation of the ASE due to the saturation characteristic in an SOA, resulting in the amplification of the signal. We investigated the high-speed response of the optical preamplifier. We used a polarization insensitive GaInAsP bulk SOA. We also investigated the improvement in receiver sensitivity of the optical preamplifier. We measured bit error rate (BER) curves with and without the optical preamplifier. The minimum receiver sensitivity was improved by about 10, 8 and 7 dB for 2.5, 5 and 10 Gb/s signal, respectively.

articleTitle: Strong amplification of femtosecond pulses in quantum dot semiconductor optical amplifier
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: We demonstrate strong amplification (>21 dB) of 200 fs pulses in a quantum-dot semiconductor amplifier. Our measurements have shown that such quantum-dot devices can amplify of femtosecond pulses in a spectral range exceeding 100 nm.

articleTitle: Collective oscillations, coherent phase locking and applications to beam steering in periodic interacting VCSEL arrays
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. Periodic arrangements of VCSEL micro-cavities separated by distances comparable to the 1/e/sup 2/ transverse length of the cavity mode intensity interact though their fringe fields. Such interactions include cross-polarization, cross-gain and cross hole burning among nearest neighbor cavities. Since each VCSEL possesses a cavity oscillation frequency the cavity array constitutes a coupled oscillator lattice admitting collective oscillation modes. Analytic derivation of the cross-coupling terms and subsequent integration of the resulting coupled rate equations, describing the dynamics of 1-D or 2-D periodic arrays of identical cavities, demonstrate that, under constant drive current and for random initial conditions, the arrays settle to a phase-locked steady state, with the same fixed phase difference /spl Delta//spl phi/ between any two neighbors. Perturbations about the steady-state propagate as collective oscillations (Bloch type modulation waves) over the array and are characterized by a given dispersion relation. A method of controlling the phase difference /spl Delta//spl phi/ is proposed, appropriate for achieving Bragg condition and beam steering, by imposing a priming current of appropriate frequency on top of the main bias current.

articleTitle: Selective nucleation control in periodical poling for quasi-phase-matched wavelength converters
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. In electric field poling, high voltage is applied to a ferroelectric crystal to reverse the polarization. Micro nuclei are generated and penetrate the crystal (nucleation), and then the domain walls move sidewise from the nucleation points (wall movement). Here we demonstrate a successful method to fabricate a periodically poled LiNbO/sub 3/ structure by separating nucleation and wall movement. In the nucleation process, high nucleation density is achieved by choosing the pulse width and pulse number. In the wall movement process, a uniform periodic structure is formed with flat domain walls. This technique can be applied to domain patterning in other ferroelectrics and could be a powerful solution to fabricating complicated domain structures such as short-period QPM devices and nano-scale nonlinear photonic crystals.

articleTitle: Direct microstructuring of fiber cores with femtosecond laser pulses
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. We have developed a novel technique, which enables us to write such structures within the bulk of an optical fiber through its cleaved face, enabling control over light subsequently exiting the fiber. We show the experimental set-up where an amplified Ti:sapphire 150 fs pulsed laser with a repetition rate of 250 kHz is used to irradiate the samples at 850 nm, via a 50X objective.

articleTitle: Use of KD*P crystals for non-degenerated broadband optical parametric chirped pulse amplification in petawatt lasers
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: The problem of creating optical parametric amplifiers of femtosecond pulses up to the multiterawatt level was fiist discussed in [l, 21. In these papers, as well as in subsequent studies [3-91, only nonlinear elements made from KDP crystals, whose aperture can be as great as 30cm, were considered as nonlinear elements for final cascades of optical parametric amplifiers (OPAs). The most promising pump source is the second harmonic of a Nd:glass laser with a wavelength of 3L3=527nm. At this pumping, the KDP crystal has two serious disadvantages: it absorbs greatly at wavelengths higher than 1200nm and has maximal gain bandwidth (1000-1200~m~[l~]) at the wavelength of signal 1050-1 1 OOnm, i.e., at degenerated (or nearly degenerated) phasematching. In this wavelength range, however, it is difficult to create light sources with pulse duration of less than 50fs.

articleTitle: Femtosecond fiber CPA system with high average power
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. The high average power femtosecond laser system consists of a passively mode-locked, diode-pumped solid-state oscillator, a fiber stretcher, an ytterbium-doped single-mode preamplifier, a ytterbium-doped low-numerical aperture large-mode-area power amplifier and a diffraction-grating compressor. As a femtosecond seed source a passively mode-locked Nd:glass laser system is used.

articleTitle: THz near-invisible materials: the dielectric properties of polystyrene foam
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. We show results on THz-TDS measurements on polystyrene foam which demonstrate that this material has dielectric properties that make it very suitable for many THz applications. We have measured the frequency-dependent extinction and refractive index of three kinds of polystyrene foam.

articleTitle: Off axis aberration compensation of focusing with spherical mirrors using deformable mirrors
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. The propagation through many optical components, and thermal effects during the amplification processes produce some spatial aberrations onto the beam. The thermal aberrations in the power amplifier (third amplification stage) are very well corrected by cooling the Ti:sapphire crystal down to 120 K where its index remains almost constant. The remaining aberrations will be corrected with a deformable mirror in order to optimise the size of the focal spot and increase the peak intensity. The deformable mirror which is already implemented in our laser chain will also be used to correct the aberrations induced by the focusing spherical mirror. The deformable mirror is silver coated.

articleTitle: Planar waveguide solid-state lasers
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. The planar waveguide geometry for solid-state lasers provides a range of capabilities intermediate between conventional rod and slab lasers with free-space resonators on the one hand and single mode fibre lasers on the other. The geometry is well matched to the natural properties of laser diode bars for pumping. Currently, the most successful active planar waveguides for high average power operation are produced by the diffusion bonding process.

articleTitle: A holey fiber based WDM wavelength converter incorporating an apodized fiber Bragg grating filter
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: We demonstrate a tunable WDM wavelength converter based on XPM in just 6 m of highly nonlinear holey fiber and incorporating a precise, compression tuned apodized fiber-grating filter. We achieve broadband 10 Gbit/s wavelength conversion (/spl sim/20 nm) with a constant pulsewidth due to short device length and correspondingly reduced pulse walk-off effects.

articleTitle: 200 mW average power UV generation at 0.193 /spl mu/m in K/sub 2/Al/sub 2/B/sub 2/O/sub 7/
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. We report the first attainment of UV generation at 0.193 /spl mu/m in KAB. This was achieved by mixing the Nd:YAG laser at 1.0642 /spl mu/m with the SFG output of the RTA OPO tuned to 0.2358 /spl mu/m. The average output power we generated at 0.2358 /spl mu/m was 0.8 W at 10 KHz. Since the polarization direction of the 0.2358 /spl mu/m beam differs 45/spl deg/ from the Nd:YAG laser fundamental beam, a 45/spl deg/ polarization rotator was placed in the Nd:YAG laser beam to coincide with the polarization directions before entering the KAB crystal. The system described has been routinely operating for more than 6 months without any damage to the KAB crystal, thus demonstrating the attractiveness of this material for UV generation below 0.2 /spl mu/m.

articleTitle: A portable eye-safe scanning aerosol lidar of the Hampton University Center for Lidar and Atmospheric Sciences Students
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. Hampton University Center for Lidar and Atmospheric Sciences Students (CLASS) team and ITT's Advanced Engineering & Sciences Division have worked together to develop a portable, eyesafe and scanning aerosol lidar system, the system is based on a 1.5 micron, 125 mJ, 20 Hz eye-safe optical parametric oscillator (OPO). Its purpose is to remotely detect aerosols, clouds, and pollution in the lower atmosphere.

articleTitle: Brillouin-induced Kerr effect in single mode optical fiber
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. We have reported the first observation of Brillouin induced Kerr effect (BIKE) in single-mode fiber. Instability of two beat signals in homodyne scheme confirms the generation of birefringence. In dispersion shifted fibre (DSF) the effect is enhanced and causes resonance in Stokes wave.

articleTitle: Phase transition theory for passive mode locking of lasers
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. Passive mode locking (PML) is an intrinsically nonlinear effect. Its nonlinear core is a saturable absorber, which favors pulses, since it attenuates them the least. Nevertheless, pulsation is achieved only when optical power reaches a certain threshold, so that the absorbers' nonlinearity is felt strongly enough. This suggests that there is a mechanism in the laser that opposes mode locking, which needs to be overcome. In this work we present a novel theory for PML with a fast saturable absorber. It is based on statistical mechanics and phase transition theory on one hand, and on known rules of the dynamics in a laser undergoing PML on the other hand. We claim that effort is needed in order to achieve mode locking since it is an ordered configuration of the modes and thus rare among all possible configuration. The quantitative measure for this rareness is entropy, and it is the balance between (generalized) energy and entropy which shapes the behavior of passively mode-locked lasers.

articleTitle: Ultrafast signal processing in quantum dot amplifiers through effective spectral holeburning
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. Significant progress has been obtained on quantum dot (QD) lasers, but the possible advantages of QD amplifiers are not yet clear. We show here that a relatively slow coupling between the optically active QD carrier states and the surrounding carrier reservoir can lead to efficient gain modulation suitable for ultrafast signal processing. The basis of this property is that the process of spectral hole burning (SHB) can become very effective. We consider a traveling wave optical amplifier consisting of the dot states, which interact with the optical signal (no inhomogeneous broadening included), and the wetting layer (WL), where current is injected. Time evolution is described by two coupled rate equations. Carrier capture from WL to dots is characterized by the capture time /spl tau//sub 0/.

articleTitle: Complex micromachines produced and driven by light
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. We describe a method which we think is most promising for the building of complex micromechanical devices, where mechanical, optical and electrical components can be readily integrated. The method is based on the photopolymerisation of light curing resins. If polymerisation is performed by a focused laser beam and the reaction is initiated by two-photon excitation, the volume in which the polymerisation reaction proceeds can be very small, i.e. high spatial resolution can be achieved. By moving the focus along a predetermined trajectory, objects of arbitrary shape can be built. The force exerted by focused laser light of the order of 10 mW intensity upon micrometer-size objects has also the right magnitude to move them, i.e. the mechanical systems can be activated by light.

articleTitle: Loss and gain measurements in the tunable UV solid state laser systems Ce:YLiF/sub 4/ and Ce:LiLuF/sub 4/
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. Continuous laser wavelength tunability of Ce: LiLuF/sub 4/ (LLF) between about 304 and 333 nm was recently obtained by pumping the crystal either with the frequency-doubled radiation of a copper-vapor or the UV radiation of a Ce:LiSAF laser. These laser results, however, raised a number of questions concerning the polarization flipping observed around 327 nm and the poor laser performance observed under /spl sigma/ polarization conditions. Time-resolved pump-probe measurements were thus performed to clarify these questions and to attempt to elucidate the role of well known detrimental effects such as excited-state absorption (ESA) into the conduction band of the crystals and/or color center formation. Our data show unambiguously that optical losses in Ce:LLF and Ce:YLF are predominantly due to absorption of laser radiation by color centers which have been produced by UV laser pumping.

articleTitle: A UV fluorescence lifetime imaging microscope to probe endogenous cellular fluorescence
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. Fluorescence lifetimes are sensitive to local physical conditions and insensitive to artifacts affecting intensity based measurements, providing a complementary source of contrast for fluorescence microscopy. While lifetime microscopy is well-developed at visible wavelengths (e.g. fluorescence resonance energy transfer between exogenous fluorophores), FLIM of endogenous fluorophores is less developed with many potential uses (e.g. biomedical diagnostics). Near UV wavelengths may become important in clinical applications because structural proteins and metabolic co-factors have excitation maxima in this wavelength region. This paper presents the construction of a FLIM system with the sensitivity to detect cellular autofluorescence.

articleTitle: Growth and characterization of GaAs/AlAs superlattices: evidence of quasi-indirect transition between minibands
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. We have grown three structures of GaAs/AlAs superlattices and characterized them by using PL spectra. Our results show that for GaAs and AlAs layer thicknesses somewhere between 50 /spl Aring/ and 20 /spl Aring/ the superlattices start to behave as quasi-indirect semiconductor materials or type II superlattices. Our results presented here serve as a first step towards eventually using type-II superlattices in optical amplifiers with reduced cross talk and Q-switched lasers.

articleTitle: Towards an apertureless electro-optic T-ray microscope
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. We use an ultrafast laser which is focused to a very small spot on a ZnTe electro optical crystal so that THz waves are only generated in this region. The idea spatial resolution is close to the focus spot size.

articleTitle: Wavelength conversion of 1.53 micron picosecond pulses in an ion-implanted multiple quantum well all-optical switch
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. This is, to our knowledge, the first report of both all-optical wavelength conversion in an Fabry Perot saturable absorber (SA) incorporating an ion-bombarded MQW SA, and fast recovery through ion-bombardment in an InGaAsP/InGaAsP MQW. The measured contrast ratio and recovery time of our device, 10 dB and 4.1 ps respectively demonstrate its potential for 40 Gbps WDM system applications.

articleTitle: Generation of vacuum-ultraviolet light by an optical contact, prism-coupled KBBF crystal
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: We generated the second harmonic of a frequency-tripled Nd:YVO/sub 4/ laser with an quasi-CW, 2.5-mW output and also the shortest-wavelength second harmonic at 172.5 nm and sum-frequency mixing at 163.3 nm by an optical contact, prism-coupled KBe/sub 2/BO/sub 3/F/sub 2/ (KBBF) crystal.

articleTitle: Using standing-wave electroabsorption modulators to generate 40 GHz optical pulses
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. We deliberately constructed electrical standing-wave patterns in the electroabsorption modulator (EAM) to increase the electro optical response and generate shorter pulses. The EAM used in this work is similar to previous traveling-wave EAMs. The geometry is shown schematically. The most significant difference is that the end of the CPW line is left open instead of terminated by a resistor.

articleTitle: Quantum dot laser diodes: physics, progress and potential
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. This tutorial is intended for those with a background in the area of diode lasers but with no specialist knowledge of quantum dot structures and lasers. The aim is to summarise the basic principles of quantum dot lasers and the current status of their development, and to assess their future potential.

articleTitle: Single transverse mode operation in a microlensed vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. We propose to integrate a partial concave mirror on top of an otherwise ordinary VCSEL device. In this scheme, a part of VCSEL laser output emitted from the VCSEL microcavity is reflected from the mirror and subsequently fed back into the microcavity. Upon re-entering, the light travels inside the cavity, with its path folded back and forth whenever encountering the high-reflection planar mirrors composing the microcavity. This allows multiple overlaps of the feedback light with the quantum well (QW) active layer. Along this passage of light, the spot size of the reflected laser beam gradually shrinks due to the focusing effect of the concave mirror until it reaches the minimum at the mirror focal length. Therefore the total field strength that the QW active layer effectively feels is much concentrated spatially toward the aperture center. This in turn results in locking laser oscillation to the fundamental transverse mode since it matches best with the accumulated reflected beam profile among the possible VCSEL modes. As a proof of concept we integrated a concave mirror, which rather looks like a microlens in shape from outside, on a GaAs/AlGaAs oxide-confined VCSEL device. Theoretical calculations were attempted based on the proposed mode stabilization mechanism. The results clearly showed the existence of mode discriminations. According to our simple calculations for the given microlensed device structure, the fundamental transverse mode (LP/sub 01/) dominates over the next higher-order mode (LP/sub 11/) by the factor of 4.

articleTitle: Optical pulse shaping using optical coherent transients
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. We present a novel method of pulse shaping using optical coherent transients (OCT's) that expands on our previous work with temporally overlapped linear frequency chirps (TOLFCs) to produce true-time delay gratings. By using multiple TOLFCs in the programming process, multiple true time delay gratings are created that can be probed using a single pulse producing multiple echo pulses at the chosen time delays.

articleTitle: 16/spl times/10 GHz multiwavelength mode locked InGaAsP laser with closed loop spectral control
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. We report on the design and development of a semiconductor optical amplifier based multiwavelength laser. This work expands upon previous efforts utilizing external cavity oscillators based on SOAs at both 830 and 1550 nm. The laser configuration is shown as a unidirectional ring cavity that comprised of 2.3 mm MQW InGaAsP SOA bulk optics.

articleTitle: Pulse generation in interferometers employing semiconductor optical amplifiers
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. Interferometers employing semiconductor optical amplifiers (SOA) have been widely used as all optical switches. Typically these switches are driven by short light pulses generated by mode-locked semiconductor lasers. This paper shows how the SOA based interferometers themselves can provide a new source of short light pulses. A SOA followed by a Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) is shown. Square wave modulated light is sent into the SOA. During the square wave rising edge, the SOA refractive index changes due to the decreasing SOA carrier number. The refractive index change causes the phase of light output from the SOA to change.

articleTitle: Powder detection using THz imaging
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. We have shown that THz imaging can detect powders inside envelopes at a concentration of 80 milligrams/cm/sup 2/ and that in a carefully controlled experiment classification algorithms can be used to differentiate between different types of powders. We have also presented images of bacteria spores inside envelopes and will demonstrate the performance of classification algorithms in detecting B. thuringiensis.

articleTitle: Phase-coded LIDAR
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. Our approach represents an important improvement to the pseudo-noise (PN) coded LIDAR technique. We modulate the laser with a bipolar phase coded PN microwave signal rather than a baseband unipolar sequence. Hence, we can use the bipolar phase codes that have been developed for microwave ranging systems. Furthermore, as we have demonstrated, the LIDAR return sign can be processed using techniques and components that are already in place for microwave ranging. These results demonstrate the principle of operation for a bipolar phase coded LIDAR with range gated vibration signature capability. While this experiment was performed at close range and a moderate PN code rate of 1.3 GHz, one could envision extending the code rate to approximately 10 Gb/s in order to obtain a range resolution on the order of 1.5 cm. Furthermore, the addition of EDFAs and telescope apertures would allow the system to range distant targets.

articleTitle: Single-mode photonic-crystal vertical cavity surface emitting laser
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. It is not easy to have stable single-mode operation from the conventional VCSEL structure due to spatial hole burning and thermal lensing. In this report, we present "photonic-crystal VCSELs" (PC-VCSELs). The PC-VCSELs are similar to standard VCSELs except that they have a photonic crystal defined by holes in the top mirror region. One photonic crystal structure has a single defect. The defect of the photonic crystal is formed at the center of the photonic crystal. In fact, we borrow the concept of the endless single-mode from photonic crystal fibers (PCF) to accomplish large single mode VCSELs.

articleTitle: Efficient and accurate computation of eye diagrams and bit error rates in a single-channel CRZ system
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. We report on the application of linearization to calculate the eye diagrams and bit error rate in a single-channel chirped return-to-zero (CRZ) system propagating over 6,100 km. We focused on this system because it is well characterized in simulations, and it is similar to a single one of the channels in some commercial WDM submarine systems.

articleTitle: Photogalvanic pulsator
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. We have observed regenerative photoinduced pulsations of optical and radio-frequency signals, generated by CW laser irradiation from Ar-ion laser in LiNbO/sub 3/:Fe. Pulsating optical scattering from the crystal has a distinct spatial structure in the form of expanding circular rings or bright crosses. Simultaneously, strong electromagnetic signals (EMS) are emitted from the crystal with bandwidth of about 1 GHz at 10% signal level. EMS was detected by an antenna-type electrode and analyzed by oscilloscope. We also have observed temporal modulation of the polarization state of cross-propagated signal beams at /spl lambda/ = 514 and 647 nm, synchronized with the EMS pulsations. Our explanation of the observed pulsations is based on self-organization of the photoinduced scattering into an array of reflection-type holographic gratings. Backscattering light waves combine with the forward pump wave, resulting in recording of the set of reflection electric-field gratings. The photogalvanic effect contributes to grating recording and creates a strong electric field along the optical axis about 50 kV/cm, which changes Bragg conditions for the holographic light scattering. This strong field also causes modulation of the probe signal laser beam due to modulation of birefringence by the electro-optic effect. As a result, strong space-charge waves are generated in the crystal, leading to the observed EMS picked-up by the antenna electrode.

articleTitle: Quadratic spatial solitons in bulk periodically poled KTP
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary from only given. We report on the generation of single and multiple quadratic spatial solitons in a different periodically poled ferroelectric which does not exhibit significant photorefractive damage and hence can be operated at room temperature, namely biaxial KTiOPO/sub 4/.

articleTitle: Nonlinear common-path interferometer using bacteriorhodopsin
publicationTitle: Summaries of Papers Presented at the Lasers and Electro-Optics. CLEO '02. Technical Diges
abstract: Summary form only given. We describe a robust single beam interferometer based on the phase contrast technique using-BR as an nonlinear medium to photoinduce the filter. We demonstrate its performance using a /spl lambda//4 optical plane and a quadratic phase object at the system's input.

articleTitle: Wavelength monitoring in widely tunable sampled-grating DBR lasers integrated with semiconductor optical amplifiers
